findings.issue: The gate is genesis-owner ONLY for all three routes, INCLUDING the two demo/fixture routes (/export, /:instanceId) that serve in-memory INS-7731 data, not the real tenant journal. This is the deliberate, documented T-0500 policy (a scoped mgmt_object:* grant must NOT open the surface) and is verified correct — but it means a legitimate 'auditor' persona is blocked until a founder-gated audit:read grant / admin tier is introduced. The file's own T-0500 doc-comment already flags that expansion as a separate founder decision, so this is a conservative (fail-safe) choice, not a defect.
findings.suggestion: No action now. When a dedicated audit-reader role is desired, extend holdsAuditRead behind a founder decision rather than opening mgmt_object:* — keep it one policy across all three routes.

findings.issue: The live-PG probe drives the DEACTIVATED-owner vector via dev-mode (x-dev-user header), not the keycloak/JWT residual-window path that the R-3 threat model actually describes. The deactivation predicate lives in loadAdminContext (mode-agnostic, ACTOR_ACTIVE_SQL), so the vector IS covered end-to-end, and the predicate itself is separately proven at resolver level by org-admin-deactivation.db.test.ts (T-0658). A keycloak-mode variant would mirror the residual-JWT scenario more literally.
findings.suggestion: Optional follow-up: add a keycloak-mode variant that authenticates a deactivated actor's still-valid token and asserts 403, to exercise extractActor's JWT branch in addition to loadAdminContext's predicate.

findings.issue: GET /api/audit was newly ADDED to the whitelist although it already had a real owner gate since T-0500. It surfaces now only because the gate was refactored into the module-scope helper requireAuditRead(), which the scan's block-scoped text scan cannot see (documented §2.4 limitation #1, same class as notification-prefs.ts's checkAdminGrant). This is an honest false-negative of the scan, not a masked gap — the cited helper genuinely gates (hand-verified + stub/live tests). Noting only that the scan structurally cannot see gates extracted into helpers.
findings.suggestion: None required. The citation is accurate; leave inline duplication out (would triple the audit-authority surface).
